sources: Shabwa Governor Awad bin al-Wazir (via SABA, Oct 20); BBC (worldrightnowlive relay); Reuters (Tribune relay); Anadolu; AP (New Indian Express)
fault_line: 58 to 73 bodies in a day: is this the war's new deadliest escalation — or does the second front only count when Washington notices?

sections.what_happened: The Shabwa training-camp toll is now 73 killed, 14 missing, 200+ wounded: Governor Awad bin al-Wazir announced the updated figure Oct 20 via Yemen's official SABA (investigative committee report), carried by BBC, Reuters, Anadolu and AP. Monday's initial figure was 53; authorities had warned it would climb. Ansar Allah military spokesman Yahya Saree confirmed the strike, claiming it targeted 'Saudi enemy gatherings' run by a Saudi officer (no evidence; Saudi no comment). Presidential Leadership Council head Rashad al-Alimi condemned and promised a 'firm response.' Reuters-verified video of the aftermath. This supersedes Al Jazeera liveblog's early 58 figure — 0600-06 HOLD is now lifted; report 73/14 missing with SABA+BBC+Reuters+AP attribution.
sections.what_verified: Four independent wire/outlet relays of the same official figure (BBC, Reuters, Anadolu, AP via NIE); governor named; SABA attribution; Reuters-verified video; Ansar Allah confirmation of the strike itself.
sections.what_disputed: Al Jazeera's liveblog still shows the earlier 58 figure (unupdated in-window); Saree's 'Saudi-run' framing is Ansar Allah-attributed, unverified. Casualty figures in Yemen remain revisable.
sections.why_matters: The number is now official and verified across four outlets: 73 recruits dead, 14 missing — the deadliest strike of the escalation, confirmed by the man who runs the province. Pair with the TRT World aftermath footage caveat (graphic) and the Saree confirmation as the attribution pair.
sections.context: Background: Yemen — RESOLUTION of 0600-06 toll conflict: 73 killed / 14 missing now corroborated by BBC, Reuters, Anadolu, AP — hold lifted to PASS

totw_analysis: Our read: The number is now official and verified across four outlets: 73 recruits dead, 14 missing — the deadliest strike of the escalation, confirmed by the man who runs the province. Pair with the TRT World aftermath footage caveat (graphic) and the Saree confirmation as the attribution pair.
